summary: Hardening batch 1 tested end to end. Backend: the offline unit suite passes (34/34). A new regression file (14 tests: health, CORS, rewrite 404/409/422/accepted_claim_ids, check 422 validation, rate-limit 429 with separate buckets via localhost fake XFF, one live prices run) passes 14/14. Frontend: SEC-6/7 head tags, char counter colors/limits, error mapping (mocked 422 short/long and 429), Reset/Undo toast, Cancel (text kept, toast, server run stopped), two full product-prices runs (live progress, gauge, highlights, 4 cards with sources, the 'cached' badge on every search row, route-badge 'Direct') and Copy corrected answer ([1][2][3] citations, sources list, toast) all pass. Only 3 live external checks were used. One environment issue: the CRA dev server was serving the OLD public/index.html (title 'Emergent | Fullstack App', posthog, theme #000000, no og/twitter/favicon) until I ran `supervisorctl restart frontend`. After the restart everything is correct.

minor.issue: The rate-limit dependency runs before body validation, so invalid requests (422) also use up the 10/10min quota. Confirmed: 10x 422 followed by 429. This may be intended, but a user who fixes a too-short answer a few times can lock themselves out.
When the client disconnects or cancels, nothing is logged. The run 'started' line has no matching end or 'cancelled' line, which makes logs harder to follow (OBS).

The updated_fact wording leaks into the rewritten text, e.g. 'The PlayStation Direct US listing shows the PlayStation 5 Digital Edition Console - 825 GB at $599.00 [1]'. VERIFY_SYSTEM should ask for updated_fact as a plain restated fact ('The PS5 Digital Edition costs $599 in the US'), not a description of the evidence.

integration_issues.issue: The dev server did not hot-reload public/index.html. The preview kept serving the old template with posthog until the frontend was restarted. Fixed by restarting; no code change. After future edits to index.html, restart the frontend.

issues: 'Generated on' uses the browser's native <input type=date> instead of a shadcn Calendar/Popover, which looks inconsistent with the dark design (minor, carried over).
Not deterministic: in one run only 3 of 4 claims were highlighted because the LLM quote was not an exact substring, so the quote was dropped. Consider a fuzzy/normalized match fallback.

action_items: Optional: exempt 4xx validation failures from the rate-limit bucket, or count only accepted requests
Optional: log when a client disconnects or cancels a run (GeneratorExit/CancelledError in run_check)
Optional: tighten VERIFY_SYSTEM so updated_fact is a plain fact sentence that reads naturally when merged into the rewrite
Optional: replace the native date input with a shadcn Calendar popover
critical_code_review_comments: client_ip falls back to xff[0] when there are <= trusted_hops entries, so a direct request (bypassing ingress) can spoof its bucket. Acceptable behind ingress only.
runs.set() stores the run at start, so /api/rewrite can be called mid-run against partial results. Consider marking the run complete and returning 409 until 'done'.
rewrite() checks req.accepted_claim_ids with `in` on a list; fine at this size.
CORS allow_origins defaults to '*' with credentials False, which is correct for this public API.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (after the frontend restart for index.html)

seed_data_creation: None. Only in-memory runs were created; rate-limit buckets used fake XFF IPs on localhost.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest tests/test_unit.py -n 0` (offline) and `pytest tests/test_hardening_batch1.py -n 0` (one live run via localhost with a fake XFF IP, so it does not use the external quota). The external /api/check bucket was used 3 times in this iteration (12:18 UTC). The Tavily cache was warm for prices queries, so runs were about 3s. The truncation notice was only verified as hidden; truncation itself is covered by the unit test test_truncation_flag.
rca of the issue: Stale index.html: public/index.html was modified at 12:13:28 but webpack-dev-server/HtmlWebpackPlugin kept the cached old template (likely an atomic file replace that the watcher missed). `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend` fixed it.
